headline: Stocks Lean Higher as Homebuilders Surge and Chips Sag After Midterm Sweep
body_html:
US stocks were modestly positive at midday Wednesday as investors weighed the Democratic sweep of Congress in the midterm elections. Of the 525 stocks we track, 319 were rising and 204 falling. Prices are not final, and the session has hours left to run.

Leadership was concentrated in housing and consumer-linked areas. Homebuilders led every group we follow with a 6.36% advance, followed by consumer names at 3.86%, healthcare at 2.95% and software at 2.37%. Materials were roughly flat at 0.06%. Semiconductors fell 3.77%, energy lost 3.01% and industrials slipped 1.09%.

The standout mover was Clear Secure, up 29.25%. The sharpest damage came in construction and electrical-infrastructure names. Sterling Infrastructure fell 18.43%, AAON 17.18% and Comfort Systems USA 15.81%. Into the close, watch whether those losses deepen or steady, and whether the rotation into housing and healthcare holds. Reuters coverage links the election result to existing worries over Iran, artificial intelligence and government debt, so headlines on those fronts could swing sentiment ahead of Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Clear Secure Leaps Nearly 30%
briefs.body: Clear Secure was the biggest gainer in our universe at midday, climbing 29.25%. The identity-technology company outpaced every other stock we track by a wide margin. With prices still in flux, the question is whether the jump holds through the afternoon.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Names Fill the Gainers List
briefs.body: Healthcare rose 2.95% as a group, and three of the six top gainers came from it. UFP Technologies gained 15.82%, Medline 14.58% and Omnicell 10.91%. The strength spanned components, distribution and automation, so it was not a single-niche move.

briefs.headline: Construction and Infrastructure Stocks Hit Hard
briefs.body: Sterling Infrastructure dropped 18.43% and Everus Construction fell 16.59%. Comfort Systems USA lost 15.81%. Together with other contractors, they dominated the decliners list. The selling was concentrated in one corner of the market, while industrials overall slid only 1.09%.

briefs.headline: Power and Cooling Equipment Makers Slump
briefs.body: Forgent Power Solutions fell 17.21%, AAON 17.18% and nVent Electric 13.73%. All three supply electrical or HVAC equipment. Their steep declines echo the weakness in construction names and make the group a focus for traders watching the close.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Lead; Trex and Nextracker Jump
briefs.body: Homebuilders were the best sector at 6.36%. Trex, a building-products maker, rose 11.78%. Solar-equipment maker Nextracker gained 11.40%. Housing-related and building-materials stocks were among the clearest beneficiaries of the day's rotation.

briefs.headline: Chips and Energy Lag as Iran Stays in Focus
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 3.77% and energy dropped 3.01%, the two weakest groups at midday. Reuters reported Iran's supreme leader saying US hostility will continue whatever party holds power. Geopolitical headlines remain a risk factor for energy into the close.
